spike_answers.a_native_oracle: NO. CLI subcommands (daemon, doctor, import, logs, mcp, plugin, config, memory, session, auth, agents, attach, auto-mode, update, gateway, remote-control) include no check/evaluate/dry-run. 'doctor' is read-only install/settings diagnostics; 'auto-mode config' prints effective classifier rules (config inspection, not a per-command oracle).
spike_answers.b_documented_semantics: YES, precise enough for honest T2: deny -> ask -> allow, first match wins, specificity irrelevant; wildcard table documented row-by-row; Bash rules match the command AS WRITTEN (git -C . push does not match 'Bash(git push *)' — the docs themselves say such rules 'aren't a security boundary around the program'); bare tool name in deny removes the tool from model context; six permission modes change semantics; built-in read-only sets are version-defined. Gaps capping at T2: stochastic auto-mode classifier, PreToolUse hooks (arbitrary code), mode overlays.

tier_evidence: No native offline decision oracle exists, but allow/ask/deny matching semantics (order, wildcards, precedence, deny-always-wins) are documented precisely enough to compute evaluations — labelled evaluation, never interrogation. (INFERENCE on DOC+REPRO)
